# pltr resource

Resource operations using foundry-platform-sdk.

Work with any filesystem resource (projects, folders, datasets, ...) by RID or by path: get metadata, list a folder, search below a folder, move to and restore from the trash, and manage markings. RIDs look like ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>; folders and projects are ri.compass.main.folder.<id>, datasets ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>.

Examples:

        # Get a resource by RID, or by path
        pltr resource get ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123
        pltr resource get-by-path "/My Space/My Project/Sales"
        # List a folder's datasets (one page; --all for every page)
        pltr resource list --folder-rid ri.compass.main.folder.abc456 --type dataset
        # Search a project for "sales" (scans its folders)
        pltr resource search "sales" --folder-rid ri.compass.main.folder.abc456
        # Trash, restore, permanently delete (asks for confirmation; --yes skips it)
        pltr resource delete ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123
        pltr resource restore ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123
        pltr resource permanently-delete ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123
        # Markings and access requirements
        pltr resource add-markings ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123 -m <MARKING_ID>
        pltr resource list-markings ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123
        pltr resource access-requirements ri.foundry.main.dataset.xyz123

13 commands. Shared options (`--profile`, `--format`, `--output`, `--yes`, paging) are left out; [index.md](../index.md) explains the labels. Every option of one command: `pltr commands show <command>`.

### pltr resource access-requirements

Show the organizations and markings a user needs to view a resource.

`pltr resource access-requirements RESOURCE_RID [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.get_access_requirements`

### pltr resource add-markings

Apply markings to a resource.

`pltr resource add-markings RESOURCE_RID --marking TEXT [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).
- `--marking`, `-m` TEXT (required; repeatable): Marking ID (repeat for several).
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.add_markings`

### pltr resource batch-get

Get several resources in one request.

`pltr resource batch-get RESOURCE_RIDS... [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RIDS...`: Resource RIDs, separated by spaces (at most 1000).
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.get_batch`

### pltr resource batch-get-by-path

Get several resources by path in one request.

`pltr resource batch-get-by-path PATHS... [OPTIONS]`

- `PATHS...`: Absolute resource paths, separated by spaces (at most 1000); quote paths that contain spaces.
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.get_by_path_batch`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).

### pltr resource get

Get a resource's metadata by RID.

`pltr resource get RESOURCE_RID [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).

### pltr resource get-by-path

Get a resource's metadata by its path.

`pltr resource get-by-path PATH [OPTIONS]`

- `PATH`: Absolute path of the resource, e.g. '/My Space/My Project/Sales' (the leading slash is optional).
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.get_by_path`

### pltr resource list

List the resources directly inside a folder (not its subfolders).

`pltr resource list [OPTIONS]`

- `--folder-rid`, `-f` TEXT: RID of the folder, project or space (default: the root folder, ri.compass.main.folder.0).
- `--type`, `-t` TEXT: Only show resources of this type: an API type name such as FOUNDRY_DATASET or COMPASS_FOLDER (case-insensitive; 'dataset' and 'folder' work too).
- paged · SDK: `filesystem.Folder.children`

### pltr resource list-markings

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).
- paged · SDK: `filesystem.Resource.markings`

### pltr resource permanently-delete

Permanently delete a resource that is in the trash. This can't be undone.

`pltr resource permanently-delete RESOURCE_RID [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).
- **destructive** (asks first; `--yes` skips) · SDK: `filesystem.Resource.permanently_delete`

### pltr resource restore

Restore a resource, and its directly trashed ancestors, from the trash.

`pltr resource restore RESOURCE_RID [OPTIONS]`

- `RESOURCE_RID`: Resource RID (ri.<service>.<instance>.<type>.<id>), for example a dataset (ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>) or a folder or project (ri.compass.main.folder.<id>).
- SDK: `filesystem.Resource.restore`

### pltr resource search

Find resources below a folder by name, path, description, RID or type.

`pltr resource search QUERY [OPTIONS]`

- `QUERY`: Text to look for (case-insensitive) in display names, paths, descriptions, RIDs and types.
- `--type`, `-t` TEXT: Only show resources of this type: an API type name such as FOUNDRY_DATASET or COMPASS_FOLDER (case-insensitive; 'dataset' and 'folder' work too).
- `--folder-rid`, `-f` TEXT: RID of the folder, project or space (default: the root folder, ri.compass.main.folder.0).
- `--limit` INTEGER: Stop after this many matches.
- `--max-folders` INTEGER (default: 1000): Stop after listing this many folders (one request per page each).
- SDK: `filesystem.Folder.children`
